proof.criterion: Architect's item 1 — refused turns, driven on Oh My Pi and claudebridge separately: three refused turns fail the claim with the provider's words in the cause and in worker-died; a clean turn between refusals resets the count; reports in order, reversed and late after the next turn all give the same run; a turn with no report counts nothing; no reminder goes after a refused turn.
proof.surface: The real supervise machine over a real Postgres claim store for the Oh My Pi backend, the claudebridge turn reporter for the Claude Code backend, and the plugin's own phase reminder under bun.
proof.command: eval "$(bash $TMPDIR/harness/up.sh)" && cd packages/daemon && go test ./internal/supervise/ -count=1 -run 'TestTheRefusedRunIsTheSameWhateverOrderTheReportsArriveIn|TestALateReportLandsInItsOwnPlaceAndFailsTheClaimAsAnInOrderOneWould|TestARunOfRefusedTurnsAtTheLimitFailsTheClaimNamingTheProvidersRefusal|TestARunOfSilentRefusalsFailsTheClaimSayingTheProviderSaidNothing|TestACleanTurnBetweenRefusalsStartsTheRunAgain|TestATurnWithNoReportCountsNothing|TestTheRefusedRunCarriesAcrossAGenerationThatResumesTheSameSession|TestTheWindowKeepsOnlyTheNewestReportsTheRunCanBeDerivedFrom|TestAReportOlderThanAFullWindowIsDropped|TestTheReportsSurviveARestartAndTheRunGoesOnFromThem' -v && go test ./internal/claudebridge/ -count=1 -v && cd ../.. && bun test packages/pi-shared/
proof.observed: All twelve supervise turn-outcome tests PASS, all fifteen claudebridge tests PASS (`TestTheBridgeReportsEveryTurnItEndsCleanAndRefusedAlike`, `TestATurnTheDaemonAbortedIsReportedClean`, `TestABridgeWithNoDaemonReportsNothingAndStillBridges` among them), and pi-shared is 96 pass, 0 fail — four more than the 92 of the round before, the refusal tests. The cause is the provider's own words: supervise/turnoutcome.go:127-129 builds `the provider refused %d turns in a row; its last refusal: %s`, and `the provider refused %d turns in a row, and said nothing about why` when it gave none. The detection is on the frame I named to the architect last round, `AgentEndMessage.stopReason === "error"`, read at pi-shared/src/phase-stall.ts:215, so no escalation to the Oh My Pi owner was needed.
proof.negativeControl: `TestATurnWithNoReportCountsNothing` and `TestACleanTurnBetweenRefusalsStartsTheRunAgain` are the two refusal controls and both pass: a turn the backend reported nothing for charges nothing, so a backend that goes quiet cannot fail a claim, and one clean turn resets the run, so three refusals must be consecutive. `TestAReportOlderThanAFullWindowIsDropped` is the third: a report older than the window cannot revive a run.

proof.criterion: Architect's item 2 — retry with no store edit: from a refusal failure, retry_or_escalate leads to a new session that gets its phase task; from an operator stop, one `legion claims retry --fresh-session` does the same; in both the old session stays recorded.
proof.surface: The real supervise machine over a real Postgres, and the shipped `legion` binary's own command surface.
proof.command: eval "$(bash $TMPDIR/harness/up.sh)" && cd packages/daemon && go test ./internal/supervise/ -count=1 -run 'TestTheRetryOfAClaimItsProviderRefusedStartsANewSession|TestARetryStartsANewSessionWhenItAsksAndResumesTheRecordedOneWhenItDoesNot' -v && go test ./cmd/legion/ -count=1 -run 'TestClaimsRetryFreshSessionStartsTheRefusedClaimInANewSession' -v
proof.observed: All PASS. A claim its provider refused out of its budget is retried into a new session without anyone editing the claims store, which is what the merge lane had to do by hand in dispatch://INFRA-264. The flag is real on the binary: cmd/legion/claims.go:216 declares `fresh-session`, and claims.go:237 sends `api.RetryRequest{FreshSession: true}`.
proof.negativeControl: `TestARetryStartsANewSessionWhenItAsksAndResumesTheRecordedOneWhenItDoesNot` is the control in one test: the same retry path resumes the recorded session when `--fresh-session` is not asked for, so the new session is the exception the flag and the refusal failure buy, not the new default — a regression that always started fresh would fail its second half.

proof.criterion: Architect's item 3 — adoption: a tester task while the implementer's turn is open is held, then adopted and sent after the turn ends; a non-task delivery adopts nothing.
proof.surface: The real supervise machine, the shim that runs the shared `jj metaedit --update-author` in the workspace, and the daemon's stream to it.
proof.observed: All seven PASS. Adoption runs inside `startSend` (supervise/delivery.go:287), so it happens per prompt actually sent and never while the agent is in a turn of its own; the shim's `TestAdoptWorkingCopyStartsTheIncomingRoleOnAFreshCommitOverADescribedOne` is the shared-workspace half, the incoming role starting on a fresh commit rather than describing the commit the previous role left, which is what keeps one role's commit from being re-authored under another.
proof.negativeControl: Two refusals from the same surface. `TestADeliveryAdoptsTheRoleIdentityBeforeThePrompt`'s second case: a working copy that cannot be adopted sends no prompt at all (prompts 0, adoptions 1), so a failed adoption withholds the task rather than letting it commit under the wrong author. `TestTheControllersTaskReachesItWithNoWorkingCopyAdopted`: the controller, which works no checkout, adopts nothing and is asked for no App identity, so adoption is not blanket.

proof.criterion: Architect's addition — the forward merge: main's own forget-session states (queued, suspended, failed, retired) won, and nothing this branch needs was lost there.
proof.surface: The supervise transition table, read in the merged tree, and its own suite.
proof.command: grep -n 'StateQueued, StateSuspended, StateFailed, StateRetired' packages/daemon/internal/supervise/table.go ; eval "$(bash $TMPDIR/harness/up.sh)" && cd packages/daemon && go test ./internal/supervise/ -count=1
proof.observed: `ok github.com/sjawhar/legion/daemon/internal/supervise`. table.go:679-680 carries the one row `onForgetSession` over the four states `StateQueued, StateSuspended, StateFailed, StateRetired`. This branch needed `failed` and `retired` — a claim its provider refused fails, and a retired one is the operator's to clear — and both are inside main's wider set, so main's resolution is a superset and nothing of this branch's need was dropped. proof.negativeControl: The table is its own control: supervise's transition table requires a row or a named ignore for every event in every state, and its table test fails the build if an event reaches a state with neither, so a merge that had dropped a state from this row would be caught rather than silently narrowing what an operator may forget.
